item.title: Connect GitHub
item.description:
The GitHub integration connects your GitHub account to Layer5 Cloud through the Layer5 GitHub App. Once connected, you can browse the repositories you granted, pick Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, Docker Compose files, and Meshery designs, and import each file as a design. The same connection can also install a pull-request snapshot workflow in your repositories.

Use it when your infrastructure already lives in Git and you want those files on the canvas without downloading and uploading them one at a time. For a one-off file, import it directly instead.

item.title: Import and Merge Designs
item.description: Import turns an existing configuration into an editable design. Kanvas identifies the format from the file content, converts it to a Meshery design, and saves it as a new design in your account. A File Upload or URL Import does not keep the original file, so exporting later produces a new file from the current design. A GitHub import is different: the design stays bound to its source, as described in Where the imported design lands.

item.title: Deploy a PHP Guestbook with Redis
item.description: In this tutorial you build the Kubernetes guestbook: a PHP frontend that writes entries to a Redis leader and reads them from Redis followers. Six manifests from the Kubernetes examples become one Kanvas design, which you deploy, inspect in Operator, scale, and remove. The application is small, but it carries the pattern behind most multi-tier systems: each tier runs as a Deployment, each tier is reached through a Service, and tiers find each other by Service name, never by Pod address.

item.title: Supported Import and Export Formats
item.description:
This page lists exactly what Kanvas accepts and produces. For the steps, see Import and Merge Designs and Export Designs.

Import 🔗

Kanvas accepts the extensions .yml, .yaml, .json, .tar, .tar.gz, .tgz, .gz, and .zip. Detection is by content and takes the first match in the order below.

Order Format Extensions Detected when Notes
1 Meshery design .yml .yaml .json The schema version is a supported design version Lossless round trip of a design file export
1 Meshery design as OCI image .tar .tgz .tar.gz .zip The archive’s layers contain a design file Only the first design is taken. Other layer files are ignored. No design file means failure.
2 Kubernetes manifest .yml .yaml One or more valid Kubernetes documents Multi-document files work. Unknown kinds are kept as generic objects.
3 Helm chart .tgz .tar.gz .gz .tar .zip A valid packaged chart An uncompressed .tar is reported as needing gzip. No values overrides.
4 Docker Compose .yml .yaml Converts as a Compose file The result is Kubernetes components.
5 Kustomize .yml .yaml (kustomization), or an archive containing kustomization.yaml The project builds Archive must contain every referenced file.

If nothing matches, the import fails and lists why each format was rejected. The interface shows only the generic failure message.
